## Purpose

Run the script `data_analysis_for_reader.R` as Quarto script to improve reproducibility.

I make tweaks to the code to improve reproducibility.

```{markdown}
## Code to follow the tutorial: "Bayesian regression modeling (for factorial designs): A tutorial"
## Authors: Michael Franke & Timo Roettger
## Date last modified: 21/06/19
## Contact: mchfranke@gmail.com; timo.b.roettger@gmail.com
```


## Set-up

Install/load packages

```{r}
pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse,  # convenience functions
  brms, # package for Bayesian regression modeling
  HDInterval, # package for credible interval computation
  # Daniela's packages:
  here, # project-relative file paths
  janitor, # convenient table summaries
  patchwork # combine plots
  )
```

Use all cores:

```{r}
# option for Bayesian regression models:
# use all available cores for parallel computing
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Set seed: 
```{r}
# set the random seed in order to make sure
# you can reproduce the same results
set.seed(1702)
```

## Load data

Some tweaks:

  - I'm re-naming their `politedata` as `df_polite` to follow my personal convention
  - using the `here` package/function
  - saving the data after downloading it
  
This chunks doesn't need to be run again:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# load the data into variable "df_polite"
df_polite = read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michael-franke/bayes_mixed_regression_tutorial/master/code/politeness_data.csv")

# save the data
write_csv(df_polite, here("01-data", "df_polite.csv"))
```

Instead load the saved data:

```{r}
df_polite <- read_csv(here("01-data", "df_polite.csv"))
```

```{r}
# inspect head of data
head(df_polite)
```

### Explore dataset

This section is my own addition.

Count observations per gender

```{markdown}
df_polite |> 
  tabyl(
    gender
  )
```

Observations per subject/context:

```{markdown}
df_polite |> 
  tabyl(
    subject, context
  ) |> 
  adorn_totals(where = c("col", "row"))
```

Semi-balanced (one participant is missing a polite context).

Look at sentences distribution.

```{markdown}
df_polite |>

  )
```

So each participant read each sentence in each context (missing polite S6 for one sentence).

Distributions of pitch

```{markdown}
# histogram
df_polite |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = pitch, fill = gender) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = .5, position = "identity") +
  theme_minimal() +

  df_polite |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = pitch, fill = gender, colour = gender) +
```

```{markdown}
# boxplot
df_polite |> 
  ggplot() +

  geom_boxplot(alpha = .5) +
  theme_minimal() +

df_polite |>
```

Distribution of mean pitch per participant (boxplot) and sentence (scatterplot):

```{markdown}
# boxplot
df_polite |> 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(pitch),
    .by = c(subject, gender, context)
  ) |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = gender, y = mean, fill = context, colour = context, shape = context) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = .5) +
  theme_minimal() +
# scatterplot
df_polite |> 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(pitch),
    .by = c(sentence, gender, context)
  ) |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = gender, y = mean, fill = context, colour = context, shape = context) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5, position = position_dodge(.5)) +
  theme_minimal() 
```

## Run and inspect model with only fixed effects

```{R}
# formula for fixed effect regression model
formula_FE = pitch ~ gender * context

# run regression model in brms
model_FE = brm(
  formula = formula_FE,
  data = df_polite,
  file = here("output", "models", "model_FE.rds"), # Daniela added this
  seed = 1702
)
```


```{R}
# print out model_FE summary
model_FE
```

This produces a warning, as `posterior_samples()` was deprecated:

```{R}
# extract posterior samples
post_samples_FE = posterior_samples(model_FE)
```

Alternative: 

```{markdown}
# extract posterior samples
post_samples_FE <- as_draws_df(model_FE)
```

Inspect

```{R}
head(post_samples_FE %>% round(1))
```

This gives us the probability that the context effect is negative (below 0):

```{R}
# proportion of negative samples for parameter b_contextpol
# this number approximates P(b_contextpol < 0 | model, data)
mean(post_samples_FE$b_contextpol < 0)
```

And the proportion of draws where politeness effect was larger than the gender effect:

```{R}
# proportion of samples for which the mean of cell 2 was larger
# than that of cell 3
# this number approximates the quantity:
# P(b_contextpol > b_genderM | model, data)
mean(post_samples_FE$b_contextpol > post_samples_FE$b_genderM)
```

So context effect > gender effect in all 4000 draws.

## Showcasing the `faintr` package

```{R}
###########################################
## showcasing the faintr package
## (still hoping for the best)
###########################################

# load package to allow installation from GitHub
library(devtools)

# install package with convenience function for Bayesian regression
# models for factorial designs from GitHub
install_github(
  repo = "michael-franke/bayes_mixed_regression_tutorial",
  subdir = "faintr")

# load the just installed package
library(faintr)

# extract posterior cell means
post_cells(model_FE)$predictor_values

# extract cell means and plot them
posterior_cell_means = post_cells(model_FE)$predictor_values %>% 
  gather(key = "parameter", value = "posterior") 

# compare cell means with each other
compare_groups(
  model = model_FE,
  lower = list(gender = "M", context = "inf"),
  higher = list(gender = "F", context = "pol")
)


get_posterior_beliefs_about_hypotheses = function(model) {
  # insert the comparisons you are interested in as strings 
  tibble(
    hypothesis = c("Female-polite < Female-informal", 
                   "Male-polite < Male-informal",
                   "Male-informal < Female-polite"),
    probability = c(
      # insert the comparisons you are interested in referring to the extracted samples
      compare_groups(
        model = model, 
        lower = list(gender = "F", context = "pol"), 
        higher = list(gender = "F", context = "inf")
      )$probability,
      compare_groups(
        model = model, 
        lower = list(gender = "M", context = "pol"), 
        higher = list(gender = "M", context = "inf")
      )$probability,
      compare_groups(
        model = model, 
        lower = list(gender = "M", context = "inf"),
        higher = list(gender = "F", context = "pol")
      )$probability 
    )
  )
}

get_posterior_beliefs_about_hypotheses(model_FE)
```

### Add prior information

```{R}
#########################
## add prior information
#########################

# see the priors of your fitted model
prior_summary(model_FE)

# get all possible priors for your model before fitting it
# (here prior_summary and get_prior give identical outputs 
# because you have not specified any priors beyond the default priors
get_prior(formula = pitch ~ gender * context,
          data = df_polite)

# define priors
priorFE <- c(
  # define a skeptical prior for the effect of context on female speakers
  prior(normal(0, 10), coef = contextpol)
)

# let's run our models with our specified priors
model_FE_prior = brm(formula = pitch ~ gender * context,
                     prior = priorFE, # add prior
                     data = df_polite,
                     control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
                     seed = 1702)

# Extract posterior beliefs about our hypotheses
get_posterior_beliefs_about_hypotheses(model_FE_prior)

###############
## model check
###############

# run model without considering gender
model_FE_noGender = brm(formula =  pitch ~ context,
                        data = df_polite,
                        control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
                        seed = 1702)

# perform posterior predictive check fo both models
pp_check(model_FE_noGender, nsample = 100)
pp_check(model_FE, nsample = 100)
```

### Models with additional random effects

```{R}
###############################################
## models with additional random effects
###############################################

# hierarchical model with the maximial RE structure licensed by the design
# (notice that factor 'gender' does not vary for a given value of variable 'subject')
model_MaxRE = brm(formula = pitch ~ gender * context +
                    (1 + gender * context | sentence) +
                    (1 + context | subject),
                  data = df_polite,
                  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
                  seed = 1702)

# Extract posterior beliefs about our hypotheses
get_posterior_beliefs_about_hypotheses(model_MaxRE)

compare_groups(
  model = model_FE, 
  lower = list(gender = "F", context = "pol"), 
  higher = list(gender = "F", context = "inf")
)

compare_groups(
  model = model_MaxRE, 
  lower = list(gender = "M", context = "pol"), 
  higher = list(gender = "M", context = "inf")
)

```
